candidate_seams.description: Treat ~/.claude (settings.json, star/unified.db, commands/, watchdog/, tasks/, star/architekt/, star/settings.json) as the managed_dir of a portable release transaction; wrap install/update/rollback of that directory with the G10 primitives.
Wrap whatever process would reload GWT/J-Space/model semantics on update.
candidate_seams.rejected_reason: explicitly out of scope (hard constraint: never touch cognition/GWT/J-Space/model semantics); also has no clean atomic filesystem boundary comparable to config/state

candidate_seams.description: Snapshot the entire ~5G ~/.claude tree (including venvs, archival snapshots, historical db backups, skill packs, conversation history) as the managed_dir.
candidate_seams.rejected_reason: not rejected on principle, but not used for this run: ~4.9G of the 5G total is reproducible/derived or archival (see fidelity_limitation below) and irrelevant to the release/update transaction boundary; a full mirror would make every gate snapshot prohibitively expensive without adding evidentiary value for H1-H12

included_in_sandbox: settings.json (1943 bytes, byte-identical to real ~/.claude/settings.json at copy time)
star/unified.db (61M, sha256 3c8059a0fc1d4711d670aa9449130c7a1ca0cc4fe4473e00a43198ec807a4d3a on both real and copy -- confirmed byte-identical)

rationale: The install/update/rollback handoff over ~/.claude's config+durable-state files (settings, unified.db, commands, watchdog, tasks, star/architekt) is the narrowest seam that (a) has a well-defined atomic filesystem boundary, (b) can be wrapped by the accepted G10 transaction primitives without modification, and (c) never requires touching cognition/agent-loop/model-semantics code, satisfying H1/H2 and the hard safety constraints of this run in one selection. The sandbox is a curated, bounded, faithful representative subset of the real ~/.claude tree rather than a full byte-identical mirror; this is an explicit fidelity limitation, not an oversight -- see fidelity_limitation below. No external/irreversible effect exists anywhere inside the selected seam (pure local filesystem), so irreversible_effect_boundaries is empty by construction for this run.

fidelity_limitation.disclosure: The sandbox managed_dir is NOT a full byte-identical mirror of ~/.claude. It is a curated, bounded, faithful representative subset covering exactly the files judged relevant to the release/update transaction boundary under test. This is reported here as a fidelity limitation per the run's explicit allowance for 'a truncated faithful stand-in... say so in the receipt as a fidelity limitation'.

excluded_from_sandbox.reason: bulk data, not part of the release/update identity boundary
historical backup copies, not live state
large, mostly static skill packs unrelated to this transaction boundary
editor undo history, not config/state identity
plugin payloads, treated as out of scope for this boundary

fidelity_limitation.verification_performed: sha256sum of star/unified.db confirmed byte-identical between real ~/.claude and the sandbox copy at copy time; real ~/.claude/settings.json mtime/permissions confirmed unchanged after the copy (original untouched, as required)
fidelity_limitation.impact_on_hypothesis_scope: H6 overhead measurements are only valid at the ~62M curated-subset scale; no extrapolation to the full ~5G tree was performed. All other hypotheses (H1-H5, H7-H13) are not size-sensitive and are unaffected by this limitation.

files_functions_lines: src/frankenstein2/self_update_transaction.py: compute_manifest, compute_state_digest, release_identity_for_payload, SelfUpdateStore, apply_transaction, apply_rollback, independent_readback
src/frankenstein2/portable_release_transaction.py: build_transaction_plan, record_attempt, ReleaseIdentity, StateLineage, TransactionPlan, AttemptReceipt (imported, unmodified)
alternatives_rejected: portable_release_readback.record_release_readback was NOT wired into independent_readback for this run. Considered as a second wrap target for P7, but self_update_transaction.independent_readback already provides a sufficient, independently-checkable readback (fresh SelfUpdateStore + recomputed on-disk digest vs persisted lineage) and adding a second wrapped primitive mid-run would have widened the seam beyond what H1/H2 call for. This is an open design point for a future iteration, not a defect in this run's evidence: record_release_readback could add a second, differently-derived readback path for stronger cross-checking, but was out of scope here.
